'''''Monstera adansonii''''', the '''Adanson's monstera''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=MOAD|taxon=Monstera adansonii|accessdate=13 July 2015}}</ref> '''Swiss cheese plant''',<ref name="WEP">{{cite book |last1=Wiersema |first1=John H. |last2=León |first2=Blanca |title=World Economic Plants: A Standard Reference |date=2016 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=9781466576810 |page=452 |edition=2nd |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AIrNBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA452 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> '''five holes plant''' or '''monkey mask plant''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] from family [[Araceae]], which is widespread across much of [[South America]] and [[Central America]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://florawww.eeb.uconn.edu/198500867.html |title=''Monstera adansonii'' Schott. |publisher=[[University of Connecticut]] |accessdate=June 4, 2013 |archive-date=May 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510190243/http://florawww.eeb.uconn.edu/198500867.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''Monstera adansonii'' is classified as a [[hemiepiphyte]] vine and can be found in [[Tropical forest|tropical forests]] with hot and high humidity conditions.<ref>{{citation |author=Andrade |first=I. M. |title=A Preliminary Study of Genetic Variation in Populations of ''Monstera adansonii'' var. ''klotzschiana'' (Araceae) from North-East Brazil, Estimated with AFLP Molecular Markers |date=2007 |journal=Annals of Botany |volume=100 |issue=6 |pages=1143–1154 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcm200 |pmc=2759243 |pmid=17823112 |last2=Mayo |first2=S. J. |last3=van den Berg |first3=C. |last4=Fay |first4=M. F. |last5=Chester |first5=M. |last6=Lexer |first6=C. |last7=Kirkup |first7=D.}}</ref> 

The common name "Swiss cheese plant" is also used for the also very often cultivated species ''[[Monstera deliciosa]]''.<ref name="WEP"/>

==Description==
[[File:Monstera Adansonii.jpg|thumb|In pot]]

''Monstera adansonii'' is known for its heart-shaped leaves. The leaves have a somewhat thick, waxy texture, and contain large, oval-shaped perforations, which led to its common name of "Swiss cheese plant". It grows to be {{Convert|3-5|ft|sigfig=1}} tall as a [[houseplant]], and up to {{Convert|13|ft}} as a vine. The Adanson's monstera is an easy to care for houseplant that likes bright, indirect sunlight, and well draining soil.<ref name="epic">{{Cite web|date=2020-02-08|title=''Monstera adansonii'': The Magnificent Monkey Mask Plant|url=https://www.epicgardening.com/monstera-adansonii/|access-date=2021-08-23|website=Epic Gardening|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-09-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210916102642/https://www.epicgardening.com/monstera-adansonii/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jyoti |first1=Asha |title=How to take care of ''Monstera adansonii'' |url=https://foodthesis.com/how-to-take-care-of-monstera-adansonii/ |website=Foodthesis |date=10 August 2021 |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=19 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230919163619/https://foodthesis.com/how-to-take-care-of-monstera-adansonii/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
There are some [[cultivar]]s with [[variegated]] leaves, including 'Archipelago'.<ref>{{cite web |title=Variegated ''Monstera adansonii'' 'Archipelago' [ Complete Care Guide ] |url=https://www.lyasolisblog.ie/home/flora/monstera-adansonii-variegata-archipelago |website=Gasworks Flora |access-date=12 February 2022 |archive-date=16 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116114834/https://www.lyasolisblog.ie/home/flora/monstera-adansonii-variegata-archipelago |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Currently, there are four recognized subspecies: ''Monstera adansonii'' subsp. ''adansonii'', ''M. adansonii'' subsp. ''blanchetii,'' ''M. adansonii'' subsp. ''klotzschiana'' and ''M. adansonii'' subsp. ''laniata.''<ref>{{citation |author=Mayo |first=Simon J. |title=''A morphometric and taxonomic study of ''Monstera'' (Araceae) in Bahia, Brazil'' |date=2013 |journal=Feddes Repertorium |volume=124 |pages=7–30 |doi=10.1002/fedr.201300019 |last2=Andrade |first2=Ivanilza M.}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Other regions this plant may be found in are the [[West Indies]], [[Antigua]], [[Grenada]], [[Saba (island)|Saba]], [[Saint Kitts|St. Kitts]], [[Guadeloupe]], [[Marie Galante]], [[Dominica]], [[Martinique]], [[Saint Lucia|St. Lucia]], [[Saint Vincent and the Grenadines|St. Vincent]], [[Tobago]], and [[Trinidad]].  The species are quite common near [[river valley]]s at lower elevations.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.saintlucianplants.com/floweringplants/araceae/monstadan/monsadan.html |title=''Monstera adansonii'' Schott, Wiener Z. Kunst |volume=4 |pages=1028–1830 |access-date=2013-06-04 |archive-date=2023-05-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510190243/http://www.saintlucianplants.com/floweringplants/araceae/monstadan/monsadan.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
